title: Import: when file headers/metadata is inaccurate, Godot will freeze infinitely trying to import the file
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.1

### System information

Godot v4.6.1.stable - Windows 10 (build 19044) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) Iris(R) Xe Graphics (Intel Corporation; 27.20.100.9664) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-1165G7 @ 2.80GHz (8 threads) - 39.84 GiB memory

### Issue description

When importing files which have headers (e.g., WAV files), Godot will loop forever trying to import the file if the internal data size is incorrect, while simultaneously blasting the console with things like:

```
WARNING: Reading less data than requested
   at: get_buffer (core/io/file_access_memory.cpp:137)
```

I think the proper thing to do here is to simply abort the import if a seek turns out to be invalid. Maybe display an alert dialog to make it quite clear to the user that a file is damaged/broken and as such is not available for use until repaired. An alternative is to repair the file and re-save on disk, but I have no idea how scalable that solution is because Godot supports a lot of import formats and trying to fix every possible problem that we may encounter sounds really difficult (although for all I know it could be easier than I realize). Although I encountered this on audio files, I imagine this could happen with any file format which has offsets or other size indications within it.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project or open an existing one.
2. Drop a broken .WAV file into the project directory. (I had about 500 of them, so that probably didn't help...). For broken files, the best way is to generate one and modify one of the chunks to report a size beyond the length of the file.
3. Godot will hang as it tries to import the file forever until forcefully terminated.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I'm not entirely certain if this requires an MRP or not. It happened with a blank project for me. The most I did was drop a (disabled) add-on into it, but that add-on does not, as far as I know, have format importers. And even if it did, I hadn't enabled it when this happened.
